footer: Privacy-first foundation · No adverse decisions by AI
ph_unavailable: Translation unavailable. Showing English for now.
home_sub: Use HELP ME to escalate a workplace concern anonymously, confidentially or with your identity on record — with anti-retaliation safeguards, evidence integrity and fair, human-reviewed process throughout.
home_ways_title: Three ways to raise a concern
home_ways_sub: Every mode keeps case-level controls, anti-retaliation safeguards and a protected mailbox. You pick the mode as the first step when you start HELP ME.
home_process_title: A fair process, step by step
home_step_1_title: Choose how much identity to share
home_step_1_text: Anonymous, confidential or identified — you stay in control at every step.
home_step_2_text: Use the guided questionnaire. The anonymity assistant may flag details that could identify you unnecessarily.
home_step_3_text: You receive a case code and a separate secret. Use them to follow progress and reply securely.
home_step_4_text: Trained staff investigate with conflict checks, purpose-bound access and a complete audit trail.
home_feat_1_text: Anti-retaliation safeguards, protection plans and scheduled check-ins follow every report.
home_feat_2_text: Reporter identity lives in an isolated vault. Case data stays in tenant-scoped storage with row-level security.
home_feat_3_text: AI is advisory only — it never decides guilt, credibility, dismissal or promotion.
home_feat_4_text: Sealed originals are scanned, hashed and kept immutable. Optional blockchain anchoring proves nothing was altered.
home_feat_5_text: Receive questions and updates through a verified, pseudonymous channel without exposing identity.
home_feat_6_text: Invite a supporter who sees only the permissions you grant — nothing unrelated to your case.
cr_subtitle: Journal entries are encrypted with AES-GCM in this browser and never leave your device. A journal is not submitted to an employer.
cr_alert_company_device: If this is a company-managed device
cr_alert_company_device_body: Employers can install monitoring tools (keyloggers, screen capture, remote backups, network logging). If you think someone involved in your concern controls IT, use a trusted personal device, a fresh browser profile or mobile data instead of corporate Wi-Fi. HELP ME cannot bypass employer surveillance.
cr_alert_device_risks_body: Entries are stored on this device only. The keys live in this browser, so clearing site data deletes them. Production storage is end-to-end encrypted, but local safety still depends on the device you choose.
cr_tip_1: Prefer a personal phone or computer you control. Avoid devices managed by the person or department you may report.
cr_tip_2: Use private or incognito windows and clear recent tabs and history after each session.
cr_tip_3: Disable browser sync for these entries; sync could upload encrypted blobs to corporate accounts.
cr_tip_4: If the device feels unsafe, consider capturing key facts offline and entering them later from a trusted device.
cr_storage_allow_label: Allow this device to keep encrypted journal entries
cr_storage_disable_hint: Disable this if the device is monitored. Entries will be removed and you can keep notes elsewhere.
cr_empty_description: Everything you write here stays encrypted on this device.
cr_decrypt_error_body: This entry could not be decrypted. The vault key may have changed or the data is corrupted.
cr_toast_storage_disabled: Storage is disabled. Enable it to save entries.
cr_toast_add_notes: Add a title and notes before saving.
mb_open_subtitle: Use the case code and the separate secret you received when you submitted your report.
mb_field_secret_hint: This is the second code you received. Keep it separate from your case code.
mb_open_error_missing_codes: Enter both your case code and your secret.
mb_new_body: Start a protected report and you will receive a case code and secret for this mailbox.
mb_subtitle: Protected two-way messages for this case. Replies are end-to-end encrypted and stay separate from your identity.
mb_conversation_subtitle: Messages from the investigation team appear here.
mb_empty_description: When the team responds, their messages will appear here.
mb_concern_alert_title: If you are being retaliated against
mb_concern_alert_body: Describe what changed since you raised your report — for example threats, demotion, exclusion or a worsened rating. A protection plan can be activated.
mb_toast_session_expired: Your secure session has expired. Enter your case code and secret again to continue.
mb_protection_support_body: Anti-retaliation safeguards apply to every report. Ask for a protection plan or invite a trusted supporter to help you follow the case.
cse_track_subtitle: Enter the case code and secret from the end of your report.
cse_open_error_failed: Could not open the case. Check your codes and try again.
cse_lost_codes_body: Your case code and secret are only shown once when you submit. Check your local journal if you saved a copy there.
cse_subtitle: Status is read directly from the platform services for this case.
cse_no_protection_plan: No active protection plan. Anti-retaliation safeguards still apply to every report.
cse_mailbox_body: Follow progress and reply securely to this case.
cse_local_copy_body: This is an encrypted copy of your report narrative stored on this device.
cse_activity_subtitle: A read-only timeline of records on this case.
cse_activity_empty_description: Staff actions will appear here as the case progresses.
crsup_subtitle: A supporter sees only what you explicitly share — never unrelated case data.
crsup_alert_open_case_body: You need an open case before you can invite a supporter.
crsup_inviting_body: The supporter sees only the permissions you grant below — nothing unrelated to your case.
crsup_field_contact_hint: A phone number or email address where the invitation can be delivered.
crsup_empty_description: Invite a family member, union representative, attorney or trusted colleague.
crsup_sealed_hint: Supporter identities are encrypted on this device and never stored in plaintext.
crsup_toast_require_fields: Add a name and a contact detail first.
emg_subtitle: If someone is in immediate danger, call the local emergency service now. These numbers are pulled live from the Emergency Number API when you open this page.
emg_locating_body: We use your browser location to show the correct numbers for where you are.
emg_locate_error_body: Choose your country below to see the correct numbers.
emg_choose_country_subtitle: Emergency numbers are usually national. Use this if your location is wrong or you are looking for another country.
emg_112_works: 112 is the common emergency number in {n}.
emg_bundled_fallback: These numbers are bundled with the app and may be out of date.
emg_verify_locally: Verify the number locally before you rely on it.
emg_danger_leave: Leave the situation if it is safe to do so, then call the emergency number.
emg_danger_112_lock: On many phones you can call 112 from the lock screen, even with no signal on your own network.
emg_danger_text911: Text-to-911 / 112 text services exist in some countries — ask your local service for availability.
emg_danger_not_service: This platform is not an emergency service and its staff cannot dispatch help.
emg_about_location_body: Your browser's location (or your network address) is sent to BigDataCloud only to find your country and city. Nothing is stored. You can choose a country manually instead and no location is used at all.
rpt_page_title: Create a protected HELP ME request
rpt_page_subtitle: You control how much identity is shared. Nothing leaves this device until you submit the final review step.
rpt_device_alert_body: If this is a company-managed device, consider using a trusted personal device or a fresh browser profile. HELP ME cannot bypass employer surveillance.
rpt_safety_tips_subtitle: Small habits that keep your session private.
rpt_tip_1: Use a device you control and a private browser window.
rpt_tip_2: Clear your browsing history and close tabs when you are done.
rpt_tip_3: Disable browser sync so encrypted data does not reach a corporate account.
rpt_tip_4: Use Quick exit to wipe this session and leave immediately.
rpt_how_raise_concern: How would you like to raise this concern?
rpt_details_subtitle: The more structured detail you give, the easier a fair review becomes.
rpt_jurisdiction_hint: The rules and timelines that apply to your concern depend on this.
rpt_approx_dates_hint: A rough window is enough — for example the month and year.
rpt_witnesses_hint: People who saw or can support what happened.
rpt_witnesses_placeholder: e.g. names or roles, separated by commas
rpt_urgent_protection: I am at immediate risk and want urgent protection.
rpt_preserve_materials: I want related materials preserved before they are changed or deleted.
rpt_contact_details_subtitle: Only for follow-up on this case. Stored in a separate vault.
rpt_rights_subtitle: General, jurisdiction-aware guidance — not legal advice.
rpt_legal_placeholder: e.g. Can my employer retaliate if I report anonymously?
rpt_not_legal_advice_body: This assistant gives general information to help you decide your options. It is not a lawyer, and its answer is not legal advice.
rpt_events_subtitle: Describe what happened in your own words.
rpt_your_account_hint: Include dates, places, people and anything you can remember. Minimum 20 characters.
rpt_pii_advice: Consider removing or generalising these so they cannot identify you.
rpt_reviewing: Reviewing your account for identifying details…
rpt_scan_advice: The scan updates automatically as you write. You decide what to change.
rpt_save_journal_copy: Save an encrypted copy to my journal
rpt_save_journal_hint: Kept locally on this device. Journal entries are not submitted.
rpt_review_submit_subtitle: Check the details before anything is sent.
rpt_what_happens_body: . A trained team reviews it with conflict checks and purpose-bound access. Your case code and secret are created now — keep them safe.
rpt_codes_shown_once: These are shown once and cannot be recovered later. Write them down somewhere private.
rpt_err_choose_category: Choose a category and write at least a short account before submitting.
rpt_err_legal_detail: Add more detail — the question needs at least 30 characters.
rpt_ai_unavailable: The guidance assistant is unavailable right now. Try again later.
mode_anon_desc: Receive a random case code and a separate secret. The platform cannot link the report back to you.
mode_conf_desc: Your identity is encrypted in a separate realm. Exceptional disclosure needs independent dual approval.
mode_iden_desc: Share your contact details for direct follow-up while keeping case-level access controls in place.
imp_mental: Impact on wellbeing or mental health
imp_career: Impact on role, pay or career
trust_title: How this platform earns your trust
trust_subtitle: The design principles behind every decision in safelytold — readable by anyone, verifiable by experts.
trust_alert_title: You never have to take our word for it
trust_alert_body: The integrity ledger, audit chain and policy decisions are all queryable through this trust centre. Anyone can verify a proof against the ledger without logging in.
trust_pillar_identity: Identity is sealed, never stored with the report
trust_pillar_identity_body: Your report travels with a case code, not your name. If you choose to store your identity, it is sealed in a separate vault that requires multi-person approval to open. The reporter identity realm is the only service that can map a case code to the vault.
trust_pillar_evidence_body: Uploads are copied into sealed storage, fingerprinted with SHA-256 and virus-scanned before investigators ever see them. The integrity ledger records a Merkle root of every evidence batch.
trust_pillar_authority: No single person can act alone
trust_pillar_authority_body: Access to a case requires the policy engine to check assignment, purpose and dual approval. Decisions that are denied, approved or recused are logged in an append-only audit chain.
trust_pillar_ledger: The chain of custody is verifiable
trust_pillar_ledger_body: Every audit batch and evidence manifest is anchored into an integrity ledger. In production the ledger is anchored to a public blockchain so any reader can verify a proof without trusting this platform.
trust_pillar_minimisation: Only what is needed, only for as long as needed
trust_pillar_minimisation_body: Purpose-bound processing is enforced by the platform: a record is accessible only to roles whose assigned purpose matches. Data is retained and deleted according to the tenant policy pack.
trust_pillar_governance: Humans are in control of automation
trust_pillar_governance_body: AI is advisory. Raw evidence is never sent to model providers, and every AI run carries a human-approval flag and an uncertainty score that an investigator must consider.
trust_verify_chain_body: Tenant audit records form a hash chain. You can ask the platform to verify the whole chain for a tenant and receive a signed result.
trust_verify_proof_body: Anchor Merkle roots are recorded per batch. With the leaf hash, the root and a proof you can confirm that an item was part of a recorded batch.
trust_reports_body: Aggregate, de-identified figures on the volume of reports and the process timeline — published only when a cohort is large enough that no individual could be inferred.
gov_subtitle: Who decides what, and under what rules. The platform encodes guardrails so that power is never unchecked.
gov_fair_process_body: Reports are treated as allegations until assessed. Findings are evidence-linked, address contrary material, and every party gets a fair chance to respond.
gov_least_privilege_body: People see only what their role and the current purpose require. Being an administrator or executive grants no standing access to case content.
gov_human_accountability_body: AI is advisory only. Accountable humans make decisions and sign findings; automation never takes an adverse action on its own.
gov_data_minimisation_body: The platform collects only what the report and the process need, keeps it only as long as needed, and applies retention rules per tenant policy.
gov_transparent_body: Access, escalation and retention rules are published and queryable through the trust centre — readable by anyone, verifiable by experts.
gov_separation_body: Investigators, reviewers and decision-makers are separate roles. No single person can both build and approve a finding.
gov_oversight_body: Senior-conflict and unsafe-route cases escalate to an independent ombuds, audit committee or board delegate under transparent rules.
integ_subtitle: The technical controls that make it possible to trust the process without trusting the reader.
integ_sealed_body: Case data is encrypted with per-case keys, wrapped by a key-management realm and only unwrapped for an approved, purpose-bound session. The database cannot be read meaningfully by a backup, a breach or an administrator.
integ_audit_body: Each audit entry is hashed together with the previous entry and signed. Re-ordering, deleting or editing any entry breaks the chain — verifiable by anyone with the first hash.
integ_anchor_body: Batches of evidence manifests, audit records and policy versions are merkle-rooted and anchored. Anchors carry hashes only — never case content — so they can be public.
integ_verify_body: Anyone can confirm that a leaf hash is genuinely contained in an anchored merkle root, using only the proof path. This is the same check the platform performs internally.
integ_provide_hash_root: Provide both a leaf hash and a Merkle root.
integ_proof_invalid_json: The proof is not valid JSON.
integ_result_valid_body: The leaf hash is contained in the anchored Merkle root.
integ_result_invalid_body: The leaf hash could not be verified against the given root.
priv_subtitle: What the platform stores, what it never stores, and how identity stays separate from your report.
priv_realms_body: Reporter identity lives in an isolated realm. No service other than the reporter identity realm can map a case code to a person.
priv_purpose_body: A record is accessible only to roles whose assigned purpose matches. Access that does not fit the declared purpose is denied and logged.
priv_reporter_body: You choose anonymous, confidential or identified. Nothing leaves your device until you submit, and you can add or remove contact details at any step.
priv_retention_body: Data is kept only as long as the tenant policy allows, then deleted. Retention and deletion rules are published in the trust centre.
priv_anon_body: — the platform cannot link the report back to you.
priv_conf_body: — your identity is encrypted in a separate realm and needs dual approval to open.
priv_iden_body: — your contact details are shared only for direct follow-up.
priv_never_label: Sell or share your personal data.
priv_never_infer: Infer your identity from evidence or metadata.
priv_never_sell: Turn your case into a reputation score.
priv_never_feed: Feed raw evidence to AI model providers.
ai_subtitle: How artificial intelligence is used — and deliberately constrained — in this platform.
ai_never_body: AI is advisory only. It never decides guilt, credibility, outcomes or career decisions, and it never sees raw evidence.
ai_cap_reporter_writing_desc: Helps a reporter draft a clear, factual narrative without coaching.
ai_cap_anonymity_scan_desc: Finds personal identifiers so a report can be safely anonymised.
ai_cap_triage_copilot_desc: Summarises a report and suggests next steps; never decides an outcome.
ai_cap_evidence_chronology_desc: Builds a timeline from redacted evidence and flags gaps.
ai_cap_policy_retrieval_desc: Answers policy questions from the supplied policy text only.
ai_cap_investigation_summary_desc: Summarises investigation state and open items, without verdicts.
ai_cap_pattern_analytics_desc: Describes patterns without attributing intent to individuals.
ai_cap_sla_remediation_desc: Identifies process delays and suggests process-level remedies.
rep_subtitle: Aggregate, de-identified figures on the reports this platform has handled.
rep_received_hint: Total reports received through HELP ME.
rep_published_hint: Categories published once at least {count} reports share them.
rep_hidden_hint: Categories too small to publish without risking identification.
rep_no_published: No category has enough reports to publish yet.
rep_rule_min: A category is published only when it holds at least {count} reports.
rep_rule_smaller: Smaller categories are withheld to protect the people in them.
rep_rule_rankings: Categories are ranked by count — never by person.
rep_rule_metrics: Only counts are shown. Narratives, names and case details are never published.
rep_withheld_body: These categories were too small to publish without risking identification.
verify_subtitle: Verify the platform without trusting it. Audit chains and ledger proofs can be checked independently.
verify_chain_body: Tenant audit records form a hash chain. You can ask the platform to verify the whole chain for a tenant and receive a signed result.
verify_chain_invalid: Invalid — the chain breaks at sequence {sequence}
wi_subtitle: Common and ranked patterns from published research on workplace misconduct reporting, their root causes and the remedies most associated with fair outcomes.
wi_privacy_body: Everything below is aggregated from published research. No data from any individual report or case on this platform is shown, and nothing can be traced back to you. Individual reports are never ranked, compared or published.
wi_takeaway_1: You can report anonymously, confidentially or identified — research shows choice increases reporting.
wi_takeaway_2: Anti-retaliation safeguards and protection plans are built into every report.
wi_takeaway_3: You receive a protected mailbox to follow progress and reply securely.
wi_takeaway_4: Your case is reviewed by people, with purpose-bound access and a full audit trail.
wi_sig_fair_hint: Reporters who receive updates and clear timelines are about twice as likely to rate the process as fair.
wi_sig_confidential_hint: Most reporters choose confidential or anonymous channels when given the option.
wi_sig_retaliation_hint: Retaliation risk rises sharply when no protection plan or follow-up is in place.
wi_type_1_note: Consistently the most-reported category in global surveys.
wi_type_2_note: Widely under-reported relative to the share who experience it.
wi_type_3: Abuse of power or unfair management
wi_type_3_note: Often overlaps with other categories and retaliation claims.
wi_type_4: Fraud, corruption or conflict of interest
wi_type_4_note: More likely to be raised in identified reports than anonymous ones.
wi_type_5_note: Usually reported only after a first concern went unanswered.
wi_type_6_note: Tends to rise in sectors with physical or regulated environments.
wi_cause_1_note: The leading reason reporters stay silent across studies.
wi_cause_2_note: People do not know where, how, or to whom they can report safely.
wi_cause_3_note: Persistent behaviour becomes treated as “the way things work”.
wi_cause_4_note: Reports often target people who control outcomes for the reporter.
wi_cause_5_note: Consequences for similar conduct vary, undermining trust in process.
wi_cause_6_note: Teams where speaking up is punished, even subtly, report less.
wi_rem_1_note: Multiple entry points — anonymous, confidential and identified.
wi_rem_2_note: Protection plans and follow-up reduce fear and increase reporting.
wi_rem_3_note: Reporters who hear back feel the process was fair.
wi_rem_4_note: Builds a culture where peers challenge unacceptable conduct.
wi_rem_5_note: Consequences applied consistently, including at senior levels.
wi_rem_6_note: Publishing anonymised trends builds confidence that reports matter.
